question: What are the minimum mounting heights for roadside signs in rural areas and in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian activity is likely?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For signs installed at the side of the road in rural areas, the minimum mounting height from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement is 5 feet. In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely to occur (or where the sign's view might be obstructed), the minimum height is 7 feet, measured to the top of the curb or, without a curb, to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way. The same 5-foot/7-foot minimums apply in temporary traffic control zones and to YIELD or STOP signs at passive grade crossings. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - "In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the top of the curb, or in the absence of curb, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For temporary traffic control: "The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road in rural areas shall be 5 feet (see Figure 6F-1)," and in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, the minimum height "shall be 7 feet (see Figure 6F-1)." - At passive grade crossings, when a Crossbuck Assembly is on a new support or a YIELD/STOP sign is on a separate support, the mounting height "shall be at least 5 feet in rural areas and shall be at least 7 feet in areas where parking or pedestrian movements are likely to occur." Guidance (recommended): - Except as otherwise provided, signs mounted on portable sign supports that do not meet the minimum mounting heights provided in Part 2 should not be used for a duration of more than 3 days. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 illustrates a rural roadside sign (STOP) with "5 ft MIN." to the bottom of the sign and a roadside sign in a business, commercial, or residential area (Speed Limit) with "7 ft MIN." where parking or pedestrian movements are likely to occur. - [Image 2] Shows Figure 6F-1 with typical temporary traffic control installations: "5 ft MIN." in rural areas (diagrams A and B) and "7 ft MIN." in business, commercial, or residential areas with and without curb (diagrams C and D). - [Image 3] Provides the full-page view of Figure 2A-2, confirming the 5 ft minimum for rural roadside signs and 7 ft minimum for urban/business area signs, along with lateral offset dimensions. - [Image 4] Shows the text of Section 2A.15 Mounting Height, including the Standard provisions establishing the 5-foot rural and 7-foot business/commercial/residential minimums. - [Image 5] Shows Figure 2M-3 for recreational and cultural interest area signs, which applies the same 7 ft minimum in business, commercial, or residential areas and 5 ft minimum in rural areas. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 6F.02 Standard §4 (p.790) - Section 6F.02 Standard §5 (p.790) - Section 8B.04 Standard §12 (p.1000) - Section 6F.02 Guidance §11 (p.791) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51)
gold_answer: The minimum is 5 feet in rural areas and 7 feet in business, commercial, or residential areas where such activity or obstruction is likely, measured as specified from the near pavement edge or curb.
